record.paper_title: Some open problems related to small divisors
record.original_question: Let M be a closed Riemannian manifold of dimension at least 2, and consider time-periodic Lagrangians of the form kinetic energy plus a potential V in C^r(M×T). Is there a residual subset of such potentials for which the associated Euler-Lagrange flow has some trajectory whose kinetic energy tends to infinity as t→∞?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed (compact, boundaryless) Riemannian manifold of dimension at least $2$, and let $\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$. For an integer $r \geq 2$ and a potential $V \in C^r(M \times \mathbb{T})$, consider the time-periodic Lagrangian
$$L_V(x, v, t) = \tfrac{1}{2}\,g_x(v,v) - V(x, t), \qquad (x,v,t) \in TM \times \mathbb{T},$$
where $g$ is the Riemannian metric on $M$. Let $\Phi^t_V$ denote the associated (time-dependent) Euler–Lagrange flow on $TM \times \mathbb{T}$, and define the kinetic energy along a trajectory $(x(t), \dot x(t))$ by $K(t) = \tfrac{1}{2}\,g_{x(t)}(\dot x(t), \dot x(t))$.

Question: Does there exist a residual subset $\mathcal{R} \subset C^r(M \times \mathbb{T})$ (in the sense of Baire category) such that for every $V \in \mathcal{R}$ the Euler–Lagrange flow of $L_V$ admits at least one trajectory $(x(t),\dot x(t))$ with
$$K(t) \longrightarrow \infty \quad \text{as} \quad t \to \infty\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: This is a well-known question of J. Mather concerning generic energy growth (a form of Arnold diffusion) for mechanical Lagrangian systems with time-periodic potentials. Partial results are known: Mather announced existence of orbits with unbounded energy growth in specific settings, and quantitative/structural results by Bolotin–Treschev, Gelfreich–Turaev, Cheng–Xue–Zhang, and others establish energy drift in particular classes (e.g., perturbations of uniformly hyperbolic systems, certain low-dimensional cases). However, the full residual/generic statement on an arbitrary closed Riemannian manifold of dimension $\geq 2$ does not appear to have been fully established in the literature, and is generally cited as still open.

status_evidence.title: Some recent developments in Arnold diffusion (Cheng–Xue)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys generic energy growth and Arnold diffusion problems originating from Mather, presenting partial results on residual sets of perturbations producing diffusing orbits.
status_evidence.claim: Mather's generic energy-growth question is treated as a guiding open problem with partial progress in special settings.

status_evidence.title: Energy growth in Hamiltonian systems (Gelfreich–Turaev)
status_evidence.snippet: Mather discovered that adding a time-periodic perturbation to the Hamiltonian of a uniformly hyperbolic flow creates orbits with unbounded energy growth.
status_evidence.claim: Energy growth orbits are constructed in special (uniformly hyperbolic) settings, supporting but not fully resolving the general residual statement.
